De 16 à 29, les nombres s’écrivent **en: From 16 to 29, numbers are written **as one word**: dieciséis, veintiuno, veinticinco. From 31 on, you use **y**: treinta **y** uno.
**uno** devient **un** devant un nom mas: **uno** becomes **un** before a masculine noun (un libro, veintiún años) and **una** before a feminine noun (veintiuna personas).
Les centaines s’accordent : doscient**os: Hundreds agree: doscient**os** euros, doscient**as** personas. **cien** on its own, but **ciento** in 101–199.
Devant un nom masculin, primero et terce: Before a masculine noun, primero and tercero lose their o: el primer día, el tercer piso.
**11-15 :** once, doce, trece, catorce,: **11–15:** once, doce, trece, catorce, quince. **16–19:** dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve. **20–29:** veinte, veintiuno, veintidós… **Tens:** treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa.
**Centaines :** cien, doscientos, tresci: **Hundreds:** cien, doscientos, trescientos, cuatrocientos, **quinientos**, seiscientos, **setecientos**, ochocientos, **novecientos**. **Thousand:** mil, dos mil. **Million:** un millón **de** euros.

L’anglais a **26 lettres**, comme le fra: English has **26 letters**, but the same letter can be pronounced in several ways: **a** in cat, name, car, all. So you have to learn words **with their sound**, by listening to them.
**Épeler** est très courant (au téléphon: **Spelling out** words is very common (on the phone, for a name): learn the names of the letters well.

**th** : la langue entre les dents, sour: **th**: tongue between the teeth, voiceless in **think**, voiced in **the**. **h**: always breathed (hello, happy) — don’t drop it! **r**: the tongue pulls back without touching the palate. **w**: a very quick “oo” (water, week).
Chaque mot a **une syllabe accentuée**,: Each word has **one stressed syllable**, louder and longer: **HO**-tel, ba-**NA**-na, **PHO**-to-graph / pho-**TO**-gra-pher. Some letters are **silent**: k in **know**, w in **write**, b in **climb**, gh in **night**.
